title: Weather cancellation with overnight duty of care
narrative: Snowstorm, flight cancelled, I was stuck overnight and paid for a hotel and dinner myself. The airline says weather means they owe me nothing at all. Is that right?

documents.content:
BOOKING BB2M91 — Passenger: H. OKONKWO (adult)
Carrier: Northwind (NW)
NW220  OSL 14 Jan 2026 18:30  ->  MAN 14 Jan 2026 20:05
Single booking reference. Great-circle distance OSL-MAN: 1,045 km.
Status: CONFIRMED. Fare paid: 96.00 units.

From: ops@northwind.example
Sent: 14 Jan 2026 16:02 UTC
Subject: NW220 cancelled

NW220 OSL-MAN on 14 Jan is cancelled. You have been rebooked on NW222 departing 15 Jan 2026 09:15.

NORTHWIND OPS LOG — NW220 / 14JAN2026
Status: CANCELLED
Cause code: WX-MIN
Cause text: OSL below operating minima. RVR 275m, freezing snow, airport departure rate reduced to zero 15:40-22:00Z. Airport authority declared ground stop.

ITEMISED RECEIPTS SUBMITTED BY PASSENGER
1. Clarion Hotel Oslo Airport, 1 night 14-15 Jan, room only .... 190.00 units (receipt no. 44812)
2. Airport restaurant, evening meal 14 Jan ................... 34.00 units (receipt no. 9911)
3. Breakfast 15 Jan .......................................... 16.00 units (receipt no. 9974)
TOTAL 240.00 units
CHECK-IN CONFIRMATION NW220 14JAN2026 — OKONKWO/H — accepted for travel 15:55Z, seat 12C. Flight subsequently cancelled.

carrier_response.text: Your claim is declined. NW220 was cancelled due to extraordinary circumstances (severe weather) outside our control. No compensation is payable and we are unable to reimburse your expenses.

derivation: S3.3(a) weather below minima -> extraordinary -> no Part 5 compensation
S6.1 duty of care owed regardless of cause
S6.2(a)+(b) overnight wait, meals and hotel
S6.3 240 units is under the 300 cap -> 240 payable
S9.1(e) rejection is silent on / refuses duty of care where S6.1 applies -> validly challengeable
